# core/p256.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/p256.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

ECDSA signatures over the curve P-256 (secp256r1) with
SHA-256: verification for the ecdsa_secp256r1_sha256 scheme of TLS 1.3
certificates (FIPS 186-4), and public keys, ECDH and signing with a caller-drawn
nonce, for the Web Crypto API.

What is proved: every access is in bounds, nothing leaks, and the numbers
the arithmetic works on have 16 limbs. Not proved: that the arithmetic is
right; the tests check signatures made by OpenSSL, many one-bit changes of
the signature, key and message being refused, and out-of-range values. The
code is not constant time: verification handles only public values, but
key generation, ECDH and signing take secrets, so their running time depends
on them and they are for programs where nobody can measure it.

A number is a `Vec[u64]` of 16 limbs of 16 bits, least significant first,
below 2^256. Products are Montgomery multiplications formed on 32-bit limbs
(a 32 by 32 bit product plus two 32-bit values fits a u64); the points are
kept in Montgomery form while they are added and doubled, and a
verification computes u1 G + u2 Q with one doubling per bit (Shamir's
trick).

`import "core/p256.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md), [core/der.bastio](core-der.md), [core/endian.bastio](core-endian.md), [core/text.bastio](core-text.md), [core/sha256.bastio](core-sha256.md).

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`ecdsa_p256_verify_digest`](#ecdsa_p256_verify_digest) | Whether `sig` is a valid ECDSA signature, under the public key `pubkey` on the curve P-256, of the message whose digest is `digest` (from any hash. |
| [`ecdsa_p256_verify`](#ecdsa_p256_verify) | Whether `sig` is a valid ECDSA signature of `msg` under the public key `pubkey`, with the curve P-256 and SHA-256. |
| [`ecdsa_p256_public_key`](#ecdsa_p256_public_key) | The public key for the private key `d` on the curve P-256. |
| [`ecdh_p256`](#ecdh_p256) | The shared secret of ECDH on the curve P-256. |
| [`ecdsa_p256_sign_digest`](#ecdsa_p256_sign_digest) | An ECDSA signature on the curve P-256 of the message whose digest is `digest` (cut to its leftmost 32 bytes when longer), with the private key `d` and the nonce `k`. |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Types and constants

### `Modulus`

```bastio
struct Modulus { m: Vec[u64], r2: Vec[u64], minv: u64, minv32: u64 }
```

Internal: a prime modulus `m` with what Montgomery multiplication needs:
`r2` is 2^512 modulo `m`, `minv` is -1/m modulo 2^16 and `minv32` is
-1/m modulo 2^32.

### `P256Point`

```bastio
struct P256Point { x: Vec[u64], y: Vec[u64], z: Vec[u64] }
```

Internal: a point in Jacobian coordinates, (X / Z^2, Y / Z^3); Z = 0 is
the point at infinity.

## Functions

### `ecdsa_p256_verify_digest`

```bastio
fn ecdsa_p256_verify_digest(pubkey: &Bytes, digest: &Bytes, sig: &Bytes) -> bool
  requires blen(digest) < 274877906944 && blen(sig) < 274877906944 && blen(pubkey) < 274877906944
```

Whether `sig` is a valid ECDSA signature, under the public key `pubkey`
on the curve P-256, of the message whose digest is `digest` (from any
hash: SHA-256, SHA-384 or SHA-512; a digest longer than 32 bytes is cut
to its leftmost 32). Encodings as in `ecdsa_p256_verify`.

Example:

```bastio
let key = balloc(65);
let digest = balloc(48);
let sig = balloc(8);
let ok = ecdsa_p256_verify_digest(key, digest, sig);
bfree(sig);
bfree(digest);
bfree(key);
if ok { return 1; }
```

### `ecdsa_p256_verify`

```bastio
fn ecdsa_p256_verify(pubkey: &Bytes, msg: &Bytes, sig: &Bytes) -> bool
  requires blen(msg) < 274877906944 && blen(sig) < 274877906944 && blen(pubkey) < 274877906944
```

Whether `sig` is a valid ECDSA signature of `msg` under the public key
`pubkey`, with the curve P-256 and SHA-256. `pubkey` is the 65 bytes of
an uncompressed point (0x04, x, y) and `sig` the DER encoding of
SEQUENCE { INTEGER r, INTEGER s } that X.509 and TLS use. A key that is
not on the curve, an `r` or `s` outside 1..n-1 and any other encoding are
refused.

Example:

```bastio
let key = balloc(65);
let msg = bfrom("hello");
let sig = balloc(8);
let ok = ecdsa_p256_verify(key, msg, sig);
bfree(sig);
bfree(msg);
bfree(key);
if ok { return 1; }
```

### `ecdsa_p256_public_key`

```bastio
fn ecdsa_p256_public_key(d: &Bytes) -> Option[Bytes]
  requires blen(d) < 274877906944
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some) == 65
```

The public key for the private key `d` on the curve P-256: the 65 bytes of an
uncompressed point (0x04, x, y). `d` is a 32-byte big-endian number that
must be in 1..n-1, else the result is None. Not constant time: the time
taken depends on the key, so use it only where nobody can measure it.

Example:

```bastio
let d = balloc(32);
let r = ecdsa_p256_public_key(d);
bfree(d);
match r {
  Option::None => { },
  Option::Some(k) => { bfree(k); },
}
```

### `ecdh_p256`

```bastio
fn ecdh_p256(d: &Bytes, peer: &Bytes) -> Option[Bytes]
  requires blen(d) < 274877906944 && blen(peer) < 274877906944
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some) == 32
```

The shared secret of ECDH on the curve P-256: the 32-byte x coordinate of
the private key `d` times the point `peer` (65 bytes, 0x04, x, y). The
result is None when `d` is not in 1..n-1 or `peer` is not on the curve.
Not constant time, as `ecdsa_p256_public_key`.

Example:

```bastio
let d = balloc(32);
let peer = balloc(65);
let r = ecdh_p256(d, peer);
bfree(peer);
bfree(d);
match r {
  Option::None => { },
  Option::Some(k) => { bfree(k); },
}
```

### `ecdsa_p256_sign_digest`

```bastio
fn ecdsa_p256_sign_digest(d: &Bytes, digest: &Bytes, k: &Bytes) -> Option[Bytes]
  requires blen(d) < 274877906944 && blen(digest) < 274877906944 && blen(k) < 274877906944
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some) == 64
```

An ECDSA signature on the curve P-256 of the message whose digest is `digest`
(cut to its leftmost 32 bytes when longer), with the private key `d` and
the nonce `k`: the 64 bytes of r then s. `d` and `k` are 32-byte big-endian
numbers; the nonce must be secret, uniformly random in 1..n-1 and used
once, or the key leaks. The result is None when `d` or `k` is not in 1..n-1
or when r or s comes out 0 (the caller then draws another `k`). Not
constant time, as `ecdsa_p256_public_key`.

Example:

```bastio
let d = balloc(32);
let k = balloc(32);
let digest = balloc(32);
let r = ecdsa_p256_sign_digest(d, digest, k);
bfree(digest);
bfree(k);
bfree(d);
match r {
  Option::None => { },
  Option::Some(s) => { bfree(s); },
}
```

## Specification functions

### `mod_ok`

```bastio
spec fn mod_ok(m: &Modulus) -> bool {
  vlen(m.m) == 16 && vlen(m.r2) == 16
}
```

Internal: the modulus has 16 limbs, like its `r2`.

## Internals

### `p256_nib`

```bastio
fn p256_nib(c: u8) -> u64
  ensures result < 16
```

Internal: the value of the hex digit `c` (0 for anything else).

### `p256_vec`

```bastio
fn p256_vec(n: u64) -> Vec[u64]
  ensures vlen(result) == 0
```

Internal: an empty vector with room for `n` limbs (so that pushing them
allocates once; if the room cannot be had, the pushes grow it as usual).

### `p256_bn_zero`

```bastio
fn p256_bn_zero() -> Vec[u64]
  ensures vlen(result) == 16
```

Internal: the number 0.

### `p256_bn_copy`

```bastio
fn p256_bn_copy(a: &Vec[u64]) -> Vec[u64]
  requires vlen(a) == 16
  ensures vlen(result) == 16
```

Internal: a copy of `a`.

### `p256_bn_small`

```bastio
fn p256_bn_small(v: u64) -> Vec[u64]
  requires v < 65536
  ensures vlen(result) == 16
```

Internal: the number `v` (below 65536).

### `p256_bn_hex`

```bastio
fn p256_bn_hex(s: Str) -> Vec[u64]
  requires slen(s) == 64
  ensures vlen(result) == 16
```

Internal: the number written as the 64 hex digits of `s`.

### `p256_bn_from_bytes`

```bastio
fn p256_bn_from_bytes(b: &Bytes, at: u64) -> Vec[u64]
  requires at + 32 <= blen(b) && at < 274877906944
  ensures vlen(result) == 16
```

Internal: the big-endian number in the 32 bytes `b[at..at+32]`.

### `p256_bn_ge`

```bastio
fn p256_bn_ge(a: &Vec[u64], b: &Vec[u64]) -> bool
  requires vlen(a) == 16 && vlen(b) == 16
```

Internal: whether `a >= b`.

### `p256_bn_eq`

```bastio
fn p256_bn_eq(a: &Vec[u64], b: &Vec[u64]) -> bool
  requires vlen(a) == 16 && vlen(b) == 16
```

Internal: whether `a == b`.

### `p256_bn_is_zero`

```bastio
fn p256_bn_is_zero(a: &Vec[u64]) -> bool
  requires vlen(a) == 16
```

Internal: whether `a == 0`.

### `p256_bn_add17`

```bastio
fn p256_bn_add17(a: &Vec[u64], b: &Vec[u64]) -> Vec[u64]
  requires vlen(a) == 16 && vlen(b) == 16
  ensures vlen(result) == 17
```

Internal: `a + b` modulo 2^256, and in the 17th limb the carry.

### `p256_bn_add_wrap`

```bastio
fn p256_bn_add_wrap(a: &Vec[u64], b: &Vec[u64]) -> Vec[u64]
  requires vlen(a) == 16 && vlen(b) == 16
  ensures vlen(result) == 16
```

Internal: `a + b` modulo 2^256.

### `p256_bn_sub_wrap`

```bastio
fn p256_bn_sub_wrap(a: &Vec[u64], b: &Vec[u64]) -> Vec[u64]
  requires vlen(a) == 16 && vlen(b) == 16
  ensures vlen(result) == 16
```

Internal: `a - b` modulo 2^256.

### `mod_add`

```bastio
fn mod_add(a: &Vec[u64], b: &Vec[u64], m: &Modulus) -> Vec[u64]
  requires vlen(a) == 16 && vlen(b) == 16 && mod_ok(m)
  ensures vlen(result) == 16
```

Internal: `a + b` modulo `m` (for `a` and `b` below `m`).

### `mod_sub`

```bastio
fn mod_sub(a: &Vec[u64], b: &Vec[u64], m: &Modulus) -> Vec[u64]
  requires vlen(a) == 16 && vlen(b) == 16 && mod_ok(m)
  ensures vlen(result) == 16
```

Internal: `a - b` modulo `m` (for `a` and `b` below `m`).

### `p256_bn_bit`

```bastio
fn p256_bn_bit(a: &Vec[u64], i: u64) -> u64
  requires vlen(a) == 16 && i < 256
  ensures result <= 1
```

Internal: bit `i` of `a` (0 or 1).

### `p256_l32`

```bastio
fn p256_l32(a: &Vec[u64], i: u64) -> u64
  requires vlen(a) == 16 && i < 8
```

Internal: limb `i` of `a` when it is read as 8 limbs of 32 bits.

### `mont_mul`

```bastio
fn mont_mul(a: &Vec[u64], b: &Vec[u64], m: &Modulus) -> Vec[u64]
  requires vlen(a) == 16 && vlen(b) == 16 && mod_ok(m)
  ensures vlen(result) == 16
```

Internal: `a * b / 2^256` modulo `m` (Montgomery multiplication, for `a`
and `b` below `m`). The numbers are kept in 16-bit limbs, but the product
is formed on 32-bit limbs: every step `t + x * y + c` with 32-bit `t`, `x`,
`y` and `c` is at most 2^64 - 1, so it fits a u64.

### `mod_mul`

```bastio
fn mod_mul(a: &Vec[u64], b: &Vec[u64], m: &Modulus) -> Vec[u64]
  requires vlen(a) == 16 && vlen(b) == 16 && mod_ok(m)
  ensures vlen(result) == 16
```

Internal: `a * b` modulo `m` (for `a` and `b` below `m`).

### `mod_new`

```bastio
fn mod_new(m: Vec[u64]) -> Modulus
  requires vlen(m) == 16
  ensures mod_ok(result)
```

Internal: the modulus for the odd number `m`.

### `mod_free`

```bastio
fn mod_free(m: Modulus)
```

Internal: frees `m`.

### `mod_pow`

```bastio
fn mod_pow(a: &Vec[u64], e: &Vec[u64], m: &Modulus) -> Vec[u64]
  requires vlen(a) == 16 && vlen(e) == 16 && mod_ok(m)
  ensures vlen(result) == 16
```

Internal: `a` to the power `e`, modulo `m` (for `a` below `m`). The
powers are kept in Montgomery form, so each step is one multiplication.

### `mod_inv`

```bastio
fn mod_inv(a: &Vec[u64], m: &Modulus) -> Vec[u64]
  requires vlen(a) == 16 && mod_ok(m)
  ensures vlen(result) == 16
```

Internal: the inverse of `a` modulo the prime `m` (0 for 0).

```bastio
fn p256_free(q: P256Point)
```

### `p256_infinity`

```bastio
fn p256_infinity() -> P256Point

```

Internal: the point at infinity.

### `p256_copy`

```bastio
fn p256_copy(q: &P256Point) -> P256Point
  requires vlen(q.x) == 16 && vlen(q.y) == 16 && vlen(q.z) == 16
  ensures vlen(result.x) == 16 && vlen(result.y) == 16 && vlen(result.z) == 16
```

Internal: a copy of `q`.

### `p256_sq`

```bastio
fn p256_sq(a: &Vec[u64], p: &Modulus) -> Vec[u64]
  requires vlen(a) == 16 && mod_ok(p)
  ensures vlen(result) == 16
```

Internal: `a * a` modulo `p`.

### `p256_msq`

```bastio
fn p256_msq(a: &Vec[u64], p: &Modulus) -> Vec[u64]
  requires vlen(a) == 16 && mod_ok(p)
  ensures vlen(result) == 16
```

Internal: `a * a / 2^256` modulo `p` (a square in Montgomery form).

### `p256_mont`

```bastio
fn p256_mont(q: &P256Point, p: &Modulus, out: bool) -> P256Point
  requires vlen(q.x) == 16 && vlen(q.y) == 16 && vlen(q.z) == 16 && mod_ok(p)
  ensures vlen(result.x) == 16 && vlen(result.y) == 16 && vlen(result.z) == 16
```

Internal: `q` with each coordinate times 2^256 modulo `p` (into
Montgomery form), or divided by it when `out` is true.

### `p256_double`

```bastio
fn p256_double(q: &P256Point, p: &Modulus) -> P256Point
  requires vlen(q.x) == 16 && vlen(q.y) == 16 && vlen(q.z) == 16 && mod_ok(p)
  ensures vlen(result.x) == 16 && vlen(result.y) == 16 && vlen(result.z) == 16
```

Internal: `2 * q`, for a point in Montgomery form (each coordinate times
2^256 modulo `p`).

### `p256_add`

```bastio
fn p256_add(q1: &P256Point, q2: &P256Point, p: &Modulus) -> P256Point
  requires vlen(q1.x) == 16 && vlen(q1.y) == 16 && vlen(q1.z) == 16
  requires vlen(q2.x) == 16 && vlen(q2.y) == 16 && vlen(q2.z) == 16 && mod_ok(p)
  ensures vlen(result.x) == 16 && vlen(result.y) == 16 && vlen(result.z) == 16
```

Internal: `q1 + q2`, for points in Montgomery form.

### `p256_mul`

```bastio
fn p256_mul(k: &Vec[u64], q: &P256Point, p: &Modulus) -> P256Point
  requires vlen(k) == 16 && vlen(q.x) == 16 && vlen(q.y) == 16 && vlen(q.z) == 16 && mod_ok(p)
  ensures vlen(result.x) == 16 && vlen(result.y) == 16 && vlen(result.z) == 16
```

Internal: `k * q`.

### `p256_mul2`

```bastio
fn p256_mul2(k1: &Vec[u64], q1: &P256Point, k2: &Vec[u64], q2: &P256Point, p: &Modulus) -> P256Point
  requires vlen(k1) == 16 && vlen(q1.x) == 16 && vlen(q1.y) == 16 && vlen(q1.z) == 16 && mod_ok(p)
  requires vlen(k2) == 16 && vlen(q2.x) == 16 && vlen(q2.y) == 16 && vlen(q2.z) == 16
  ensures vlen(result.x) == 16 && vlen(result.y) == 16 && vlen(result.z) == 16
```

Internal: `k1 * q1 + k2 * q2`, with one doubling per bit for both
(Shamir's trick).

### `p256_on_curve`

```bastio
fn p256_on_curve(x: &Vec[u64], y: &Vec[u64], p: &Modulus) -> bool
  requires vlen(x) == 16 && vlen(y) == 16 && mod_ok(p)
```

Internal: whether (x, y) is on the curve y^2 = x^3 - 3x + b, with both
coordinates below `p`.

### `p256_der_uint`

```bastio
fn p256_der_uint(sig: &Bytes, start: u64, end: u64) -> Option[Bytes]
  requires start <= end && end <= blen(sig)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some) == 32
```

Internal: the signature number in the INTEGER `item` of `sig` as 32
bytes, if it is a positive DER integer of at most 256 bits in the shortest
form.

### `p256_verify_numbers`

```bastio
fn p256_verify_numbers(qx: &Vec[u64], qy: &Vec[u64], e: &Vec[u64], r: &Vec[u64], s: &Vec[u64]) -> bool
  requires vlen(qx) == 16 && vlen(qy) == 16 && vlen(e) == 16 && vlen(r) == 16 && vlen(s) == 16
```

Internal: checks the signature (`r`, `s`) of the hash `e` under the key
(`qx`, `qy`), all as numbers.

### `p256_hash_number`

```bastio
fn p256_hash_number(d: &Bytes) -> Vec[u64]
  ensures vlen(result) == 16
```

Internal: the first 32 bytes of the digest `d` (as a number), or `d`
itself with leading zeros when it is shorter (FIPS 186-4 6.4: a longer
hash is cut to the leftmost bits of the order's length).

### `p256_bn_put`

```bastio
fn p256_bn_put(a: &Vec[u64], out: &mut Bytes, at: u64)
  requires vlen(a) == 16 && at + 32 <= blen(out) && at < 274877906944
  ensures blen(out) == blen(old(out))
```

Internal: writes the number `a` as 32 big-endian bytes at `out[at..at+32]`.

### `p256_affine`

```bastio
fn p256_affine(q: &P256Point, p: &Modulus) -> Option[Bytes]
  requires vlen(q.x) == 16 && vlen(q.y) == 16 && vlen(q.z) == 16 && mod_ok(p)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some) == 64
```

Internal: the affine coordinates of `q` as 32 bytes of x and 32 bytes of
y, or None for the point at infinity.

### `p256_base`

```bastio
fn p256_base() -> P256Point
  ensures vlen(result.x) == 16 && vlen(result.y) == 16 && vlen(result.z) == 16
```

Internal: the base point of the curve.
